exposure: birth weight (extremely low, very low, low, normal)
no iron intake by mother during pregnancy
cohort: The study included 220 newborns admitted to the Neonatal Unit of Maiwand Teaching Hospital in Kabul City, Afghanistan.
finding: Neonatal anemia was significantly associated with lower mean neonatal birth weight and gestational age, preterm birth, male sex, higher CRP levels, neonatal sepsis, older maternal age, cesarean delivery, no maternal iron consumption, antepartum hemorrhage, and poor household income.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was significantly associated with an increased risk of neonatal anemia (OR=3.4, P = 0.00).
followup_time: Around 10-11 days after birth (mean age of neonates at observation)
birth_weight: Ranged from extremely low birth weight to normal birth weight, with a mean of 2516.18 g in anemic neonates and 2749.62 g in non-anemic neonates.
gest_age: Ranged from preterm to term, with a mean of 35.47 weeks in anemic neonates and 37.4 weeks in non-anemic neonates.
